skill.description: Set up Runheed error reporting for FastAPI, Django, Flask, Celery, or Python scripts. Verify a test event and connect a coding agent through MCP.

skill.author: getrunheed

security_audit.summary: Most backtick matches are Markdown, and the framework links are documentation. Confirmed concerns include remote setup guidance, a wheel without an integrity check, weak DSN handling, and an authenticated MCP connection without scope review. No evidence of deliberate exfiltration or audit-directed prompt injection was found in the reviewed skill.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to paste the DSN and suggests loading it from a local environment file.
remediation.suggestion: Have users set RUNHEED_DSN through their secret manager. Do not request, display, or read the value during setup. Keep any local secret file out of version control.

remediation.issue: Local and deployment installs use a direct wheel URL without verifying the artifact.
remediation.suggestion: Document a trusted package source and a reviewed artifact hash. Enforce hash verification for local and deployment installs, and obtain approval before adding the dependency.

remediation.issue: The fallback setup reference can change outside the reviewed skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Use a revision-pinned reference when available. Treat remote instructions as untrusted and require review before running commands or changing configuration.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require review of exception data or MCP access.
remediation.suggestion: Document which data the SDK sends and which projects the MCP account can access. Require approval before connecting, and verify redaction and access limits in staging.

remediation.issue: The verification step permits a temporary failing web route without stating where it can run.
remediation.suggestion: Use a local script or an isolated staging environment with a synthetic exception. Do not add an intentional failure route to a public deployment.

content.user_title: Set Up Runheed Error Reporting for Python
content.value_statement: Python errors can go unreported when web handlers and background jobs use different exception paths. This skill guides SDK setup, test verification, and MCP connection for error review.
actual_capabilities: Guide installation of the Runheed Python SDK and addition of the dependency to project metadata.
Initialize the SDK using RUNHEED_DSN supplied by the application environment.
Point to the framework hooks for FastAPI, Django, and Flask.
Explain Celery worker initialization and explicit exception capture for other background jobs.
Verify that a test exception appears in the Runheed dashboard.
Guide Claude Code and Cursor MCP setup for access to reported errors.
limitations: Project creation and authentication require a user with a Runheed account.
Framework integration details are linked rather than included in the skill.
The skill does not document SDK payload fields, redaction settings, or MCP access limits.
Runheed setup does not diagnose or fix the errors it reports.

use_cases.description: Identify where to initialize the SDK and add the exception hook in a Python web service.

use_cases.description: Plan reporting for Celery workers and identify scripts that need explicit exception capture.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Add monitoring to a FastAPI project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Outline the Runheed setup for this FastAPI app. Identify the configuration I must provide, but do not read or request the DSN value.

prompt_templates.title: Locate Django Integration Points
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review an existing Django application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Django startup and middleware settings for Runheed. Propose changes without installing packages or editing deployment configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Review Background Job Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Compare Celery worker errors with scheduled script failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify where Runheed should initialize in Celery workers and where scheduled scripts need explicit exception capture. Propose a synthetic staging test.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Staged Rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review the dependency, exception data, and remote agent connection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a staging rollout plan for Runheed. Include dependency verification, exception data review, dashboard confirmation, and approval before registering the MCP server.

output_examples.input: What does this Django service need before it can report request failures?
output: Set the project DSN in the service environment and initialize the SDK during startup.
Place the Runheed middleware last in the Django middleware list, as the skill directs.
Verify that a synthetic exception appears in the dashboard using a staging environment.

output_examples.input: How should we report Celery failures and scheduled script errors?
output: Initialize Runheed in the Celery worker process for task failure reporting.
Add explicit exception capture to the scheduled scripts that need reporting.
Check each reporting path with a synthetic staging error.

best_practices: Set the DSN through a secret manager or the service environment without sharing its value in chat.
Verify the SDK artifact and review exception data before enabling reporting in production.
Use synthetic staging errors and review project access before authenticating the MCP client.
anti_patterns: Pasting a live DSN into an agent conversation or committing it to the repository.
Assuming initialization alone covers request handlers or every background job.
Deploying a temporary failure route to a public service to test reporting.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks does the skill cover?
faq.answer: It points to FastAPI, Django, and Flask hooks. It also covers Celery worker initialization and manual capture in scripts.

faq.question: Where should I put the Runheed DSN?
faq.answer: Set RUNHEED_DSN in the service environment or through your hosting provider's secret manager. Do not paste the value into chat or commit it.

faq.question: Does SDK initialization capture web request errors on its own?
faq.answer: The skill says to add the framework hook after initialization so exceptions in request handlers are reported.

faq.question: Do I need a flush step after capturing an exception?
faq.answer: The skill states that the SDK sends the event before the capture call returns. It does not prescribe a separate flush step.

faq.question: Can I verify reporting before connecting an agent?
faq.answer: Yes. Send a synthetic exception from staging and check for it in the Runheed dashboard before configuring MCP.

faq.question: Which MCP clients have setup instructions?
faq.answer: The skill provides steps for Claude Code and Cursor. It directs users of other clients to the Runheed connection guide.
